slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce the lesson's 60-house illustrative dataset (np.random.default_rng(42), price = 50 + 0.12*size + noise) and fit sklearn's LinearRegression against it, comparing the model's learned slope/intercept to a hand-written if/elif rule-based pricing function on the same 3 test sizes; then list 4 real problems you can think of from your own interests and classify each as supervised (with its feature(s) and target) or unsupervised (with no target), writing one sentence justifying each label.
slots.deliverable: A fitted LinearRegression model with printed coef_/intercept_ compared side-by-side against a hand-written rule function on 3 test inputs, plus a written supervised/unsupervised classification with justification for 4 real problems of your choosing.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick one real public tabular dataset (not the course's illustrative housing or churn data) and write out, before touching code, the full ML workflow as a numbered checklist specific to that dataset: the business question, the target column, the train/test split plan, candidate models, and the evaluation metric; then execute just the first 2 steps in code (load the data, confirm the target column and its distribution).
slots.deliverable: A written, dataset-specific ML workflow checklist (question, target, split plan, candidate models, metric) plus code that loads the chosen real dataset and confirms its target column's distribution.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce the lesson's make_moons(n_samples=400, noise=0.35) dataset and sweep a DecisionTreeClassifier's max_depth from 1 to 15, plotting training accuracy against held-out accuracy at every depth to find the point where the two curves diverge, then write down which depth values are underfitting (both scores poor), which are the good-fit sweet spot, and which are overfitting (large train/test gap), citing the actual accuracy numbers from your run.
slots.deliverable: A plotted train-vs-test accuracy curve across max_depth values 1-15, with a written diagnosis (underfit / good fit / overfit range) citing the specific accuracy numbers that mark each zone.

slots.practicalActivity: By hand in NumPy (no sklearn), implement mean squared error for a simple slope-only model on the lesson's housing-style data, then write a basic gradient descent loop that updates the slope a fixed number of iterations, printing the loss every 10 steps to show it decreasing, and compare your by-hand-learned slope to what LinearRegression.fit() finds on the same data.
slots.deliverable: A from-scratch NumPy gradient-descent loop with a printed decreasing-loss trace, and a final learned slope compared numerically against scikit-learn's LinearRegression fit on the same data.

slots.practicalActivity: On a real dataset of your choice, create a proper 3-way split (train/validation/test) using train_test_split twice with stratify on the target, confirming in code that the class balance (or target mean, for regression) is nearly identical across all 3 sets, then explain in writing why the test set must never be touched until the very end, referencing what would go wrong if you tuned on it.
slots.deliverable: A 3-way stratified train/validation/test split on a real dataset with printed class-balance confirmation across all 3 sets, plus a written explanation of why the test set stays sealed until final evaluation.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce both of the lesson's leakage demonstrations: the leaky refund_issued churn feature that pushes test accuracy from 0.722 to 0.963, and the select-features-before-vs-after-split experiment on pure-noise labels (0.787 leaky vs. 0.51 honest mean accuracy over 30 runs); then audit a real dataset of your own for at least one column that fails the 'will I know this at prediction time?' test, and write down why.
slots.deliverable: Both reproduced leakage demonstrations with their before/after accuracy numbers, plus a written leakage audit identifying at least one at-risk column in a real dataset of your choosing and why it fails the prediction-time test.

slots.practicalActivity: On a real dataset with at least 2 categorical columns and 2 numeric columns, apply OneHotEncoder(drop="first") to the categoricals and compare it against a quick ordinal/LabelEncoder pass to see the shape difference, then apply StandardScaler to the numeric columns and plot a before/after histogram of one column to show the distribution shape is unchanged but the scale is now centered at 0 with unit variance; fit every encoder/scaler on training rows only.
slots.deliverable: A one-hot-encoded feature set compared against an ordinal-encoded version (with shape difference noted), plus a before/after histogram showing a numeric column correctly standardized using only training-fitted parameters.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same real dataset, engineer at least 3 new features (a ratio between 2 existing numeric columns, a binned/bucketed version of a continuous column, and an interaction term multiplying 2 columns together), fit a baseline model with and without the new features to see whether cross-validated score improves, then run SelectKBest (fit on training data only) to rank all features and report which of your 3 new ones made the top half.
slots.deliverable: 3 newly engineered features with a before/after cross-validated score comparison, plus a SelectKBest ranking (fit on training data only) showing where the new features landed.

slots.practicalActivity: Data Preparation practice lab: build one single scikit-learn ColumnTransformer + Pipeline that handles a real dataset's missing values, categorical encoding, and numeric scaling together in the correct train-only-fit order, fit it inside a 5-fold cross_val_score call on a simple baseline model, and confirm no leakage by checking that re-running with a different random_state still gives a similar score.
slots.deliverable: One working ColumnTransformer + Pipeline combining imputation, encoding, and scaling, validated with 5-fold cross-validation and a repeat run at a different random_state showing a stable score.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce the lesson's 60-house dataset (price = 50000 + 120*sqft + noise) and fit LinearRegression, confirming the recovered intercept/slope are close to the true 50000/120 built into the data, plot the scatter plus fitted crimson line, compute R² with model.score(), and then predict the price for a 1500 sqft house, comparing your result to the lesson's $225,011 prediction.
slots.deliverable: A fitted LinearRegression with printed intercept_/coef_ close to the true generating values, a scatter-plus-fit-line chart, a computed R², and a specific dollar prediction for a 1500 sqft house.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the housing dataset with 2 more illustrative numeric features (e.g. number of bedrooms and age of house, each with a built-in true coefficient you choose), fit LinearRegression with all 3 features, and compare the multi-feature R² against last slot's single-feature R² to show the improvement, then interpret each coefficient's sign and magnitude in a written sentence.
slots.deliverable: A multiple-regression model fit on 3+ features with an R² improvement reported against the single-feature baseline, plus a written sentence interpreting each coefficient's sign and size.

slots.practicalActivity: Add 10 extra noise (uninformative) columns to the multiple-regression dataset from last slot, fit plain LinearRegression, Ridge, and Lasso on the inflated feature set, and compare how many of Lasso's coefficients shrink to exactly zero versus Ridge's smaller-but-nonzero coefficients; then compute and report MAE, RMSE, and R² for all 3 models on a held-out split, explaining in one sentence which metric best captures the cost of a large single error for this problem.
slots.deliverable: A 3-way coefficient comparison (plain, Ridge, Lasso) on a noise-inflated feature set showing Lasso's zeroed-out coefficients, plus MAE/RMSE/R² reported for all 3 models with a written note on which metric fits the problem.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce a churn-style illustrative dataset (tenure, support calls, monthly charge predicting a binary churned outcome) and fit LogisticRegression, printing the predicted probability (not just the class) for 3 specific example customers you construct by hand, then plot the sigmoid-shaped probability curve against one feature (holding others at their mean) to show how the model turns a linear score into a 0-1 probability.
slots.deliverable: A fitted LogisticRegression with predicted churn probabilities (not just labels) for 3 hand-built example customers, plus a plotted sigmoid probability curve against one feature.

slots.practicalActivity: Regression practice lab: on a real dataset with a numeric target (e.g. a public housing-price or insurance-cost dataset), run the full regression workflow end to end: engineer at least one new feature, fit and compare plain linear regression against Ridge and Lasso, report MAE/RMSE/R² for each on a held-out test set, and write a 2-3 sentence conclusion naming the best model and why.
slots.deliverable: One complete regression comparison (linear vs. Ridge vs. Lasso) on a real numeric-target dataset with MAE/RMSE/R² reported for each, plus a written 2-3 sentence conclusion naming the best model.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce the lesson's 800-customer illustrative churn dataset (tenure, support_calls, monthly_charge) and fit a DecisionTreeClassifier with max_depth=3, plot it with plot_tree(filled=True), trace one specific customer's path through the tree by hand to its leaf prediction, then fit an unrestricted tree on the same data and compare its perfect training accuracy against its worse test accuracy to confirm the overfitting the lesson describes.
slots.deliverable: A plotted, depth-limited decision tree with one customer's prediction path traced by hand, plus a documented train-vs-test accuracy comparison showing the unrestricted tree's overfitting.

slots.practicalActivity: Load scikit-learn's bundled load_breast_cancer dataset and reproduce the lesson's single-tree-vs-forest comparison (tree test accuracy ~0.906 vs. forest ~0.953), set oob_score=True and compare the OOB estimate to the held-out test score, then sweep n_estimators across [1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200] with 5-fold cross-validation and plot accuracy against tree count to find where the curve flattens.
slots.deliverable: A single-tree-vs-random-forest accuracy comparison on the breast cancer dataset with an OOB score reported alongside the test score, plus a plotted accuracy-vs-n_estimators curve showing where more trees stop helping.

slots.practicalActivity: On the random forest you fit last slot, extract and plot feature_importances_ as a sorted horizontal bar chart to name the top 3 most predictive features; then fit a KNeighborsClassifier and a GaussianNB on the same data, compare their test accuracy against the forest's, and write 2-3 sentences on which model you'd deploy and why, considering accuracy, interpretability, and prediction speed.
slots.deliverable: A sorted feature-importance bar chart naming the top 3 predictive features, plus a 3-way accuracy comparison (forest vs. KNN vs. Naive Bayes) with a written recommendation and reasoning.

slots.practicalActivity: Take a real dataset with no target column (or drop the target from one you have), standardize its numeric features, and before running any clustering algorithm, write down in plain words what you expect a 'natural group' of rows to look like in this specific data (e.g. 'low-tenure, high-ticket customers'), so you have a hypothesis to check once you actually cluster it in the next lessons.
slots.deliverable: A standardized, target-free real dataset ready for clustering, plus a written hypothesis describing what a meaningful natural group should look like in that specific data.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce the lesson's 3-blob illustrative customer dataset (annual_spend, visits_per_month) and fit KMeans(n_clusters=3, init="k-means++", n_init=10), inverse-transform the scaled centers back to real units and report them, then force init="random", n_init=1 across 4 different seeds to reproduce the lesson's finding that one seed gets stuck at a much worse inertia, confirming why k-means++ and n_init matter.
slots.deliverable: A fitted k-means model with its 3 cluster centers reported in real (inverse-transformed) units, plus a 4-seed random-init comparison showing at least one bad local optimum and explaining why the defaults protect against it.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same clustering dataset, fit KMeans for k = 2 through 8, plot the elbow curve of inertia against k, and separately compute the silhouette score for each k, then write down whether the elbow and silhouette methods agree on the best k, and which one you'd trust more for this specific data.
slots.deliverable: An elbow-method inertia plot and a silhouette-score plot across k=2-8 for the same dataset, plus a written comparison of what each method recommends and which you'd trust.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same clustering dataset, fit AgglomerativeClustering and plot a dendrogram with scipy's linkage/dendrogram to visually confirm the number of clusters matches what k-means and the elbow/silhouette methods suggested; then reproduce the PCA lesson's 6-column, 2-hidden-factor illustrative dataset, fit PCA on standardized data, confirm the first 2 components explain over 90% of variance via explained_variance_ratio_.cumsum(), and name each component using its loadings.
slots.deliverable: A dendrogram from hierarchical clustering compared against the earlier k-means cluster count, plus a PCA fit on the 6-feature dataset with a reported cumulative explained-variance curve and named components based on their loadings.

slots.practicalActivity: Unsupervised Learning practice lab: on a real dataset with no label, standardize the features, use the elbow and silhouette methods together to choose k, fit final k-means clusters, profile each cluster's mean values per feature in a summary table, then run PCA to 2 components and make a scatter plot of the clusters colored by their k-means label in PCA space, writing a one-paragraph profile of each cluster in plain business language.
slots.deliverable: A chosen-k k-means clustering on a real dataset with a per-cluster profile table, a 2D PCA scatter plot colored by cluster, and a written one-paragraph plain-language profile for each cluster.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: Build Your First Models

slots.practicalActivity: Build the capstone's make_churn_data() generator (2000 customers with tenure, monthly_charges, support_calls, contract, autopay, churned, and planted missing monthly_charges), confirm the baseline churn rate of about 0.344, run the targeted exploration by contract type and churn status, create a stratified 80/20 train/test split, and fit a DummyClassifier baseline to confirm it scores 0.5 ROC AUC, exactly as the lesson walks through -- or repeat the same steps end to end on a real classification dataset of your own.
slots.deliverable: The generated or chosen classification dataset with a confirmed baseline churn/outcome rate, a stratified train/test split with matching class balance reported, and a DummyClassifier baseline score to beat.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one leakage-safe ColumnTransformer + Pipeline that imputes, scales, and one-hot encodes your capstone features, compare logistic regression, a shallow decision tree, and a random forest with 5-fold stratified cross-validation on ROC AUC (training data only), tune the most promising model with GridSearchCV, and read either its coefficients or its feature_importances_ to confirm they match the patterns you found during exploration.
slots.deliverable: One leakage-safe preprocessing pipeline, a 3-model cross-validated ROC AUC comparison table, a tuned final model via GridSearchCV, and its printed coefficients or feature importances checked against earlier exploratory findings.

slots.practicalActivity: Evaluate your final model on the sealed test set exactly once (ROC AUC, accuracy, confusion matrix), sweep 2-3 decision thresholds to show the precision/recall trade-off and recommend one based on a stated business cost assumption, add a k-means customer-segmentation lens with a per-segment churn profile, then write the README-style portfolio package (problem, data, approach, results, recommendation, limitations, next steps).
slots.deliverable: A one-time sealed-test-set evaluation (ROC AUC, confusion matrix), a threshold recommendation backed by a precision/recall trade-off table, a k-means segment-profile table, and a written README-style portfolio package covering problem through limitations.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can frame a real prediction problem, split and prepare data without leakage, fit and compare linear, tree-based, and instance-based models for both regression and classification, cluster and reduce dimensionality with k-means/hierarchical clustering/PCA, diagnose overfitting with train-vs-held-out curves, and evaluate and present a model's results -- the core algorithmic toolkit that Applied Machine Learning then takes into a production-minded scikit-learn workflow.
